en.name: Managed environments for food
en.description: Explain how and why food and fibre are produced in managed environments - greenhouses, irrigated fields, orchards, feedlots, aquaculture ponds and plantations - to control conditions, increase yield, protect crops and animals, and manage sustainability

pt-BR.name: Gestão de riscos naturais
pt-BR.description: Descrever como ambientes e comunidades são geridos para reduzir os efeitos de riscos naturais e eventos climáticos severos, como incêndios florestais, enchentes, secas e ciclones, e as consequências desses eventos.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Managing natural hazards
en.description: Describe how environments and communities are managed to reduce the impacts of natural hazards and severe weather events such as bushfires, floods, droughts and cyclones, and the consequences of these events (e.g. in Australia)

pt-BR.name: Como as pessoas moldam os lugares
pt-BR.description: Descrever a influência de pessoas, incluindo povos originários e pessoas de outros países, nas características de um lugar.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: People shaping places
en.description: Describe the influence of people, including First Nations Australians and people in other countries, on the characteristics of a place

pt-BR.name: Como os países se conectam
pt-BR.description: Descrever as ligações de um país com outros por migração, ajuda, turismo e cultura, e como essas ligações transformam pessoas e lugares.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: How countries are interconnected
en.description: Describe a country's interconnections with other countries through migration, aid, tourism and culture (e.g. Australia's), and how these interconnections change people and places

pt-BR.name: Lugares da região da Ásia
pt-BR.description: Descrever a diversidade geográfica e a localização de lugares da região da Ásia e sua posição em relação ao próprio país.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Places in the Asia region
en.description: Describe the geographical diversity and location of places in the Asia region and its location in relation to their own country (e.g. Australia)

pt-BR.name: A descoberta da tumba de Tutancâmon
pt-BR.description: Entender que conhecemos o Egito Antigo porque arqueólogos estudam objetos preservados há milênios, e que uma das maiores descobertas foi a tumba de Tutancâmon, encontrada por Howard Carter em 1922, cheia de tesouros de ouro.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Discovering Tutankhamun's Tomb
en.description: Understand that we know about ancient Egypt because archaeologists have dug up and studied objects buried in the sand for thousands of years - and that one of the most exciting discoveries ever was when Howard Carter found the hidden tomb of Tutankhamun in 1922, filled with golden treasures

pt-BR.name: Deuses egípcios e vida após a morte
pt-BR.description: Entender que os antigos egípcios acreditavam em muitos deuses e numa vida após a morte, e por isso preparavam os corpos e enchiam as tumbas de comida, joias e objetos preciosos.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Egyptian Gods and the Afterlife
en.description: Understand that the ancient Egyptians believed in many gods and goddesses and believed that life continued after death in a wonderful afterlife - which is why they took great care to prepare bodies and fill tombs with food, jewellery, and precious objects for the dead person to use

pt-BR.name: Egito, o Nilo e o deserto
pt-BR.description: Localizar o Egito no mapa da África e entender que, num país quente e seco, o rio Nilo trazia água e solo fértil, o que permitiu produzir alimentos e construir uma das primeiras grandes civilizações.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Egypt, the Nile, and the Desert
en.description: Locate Egypt on a map of Africa and understand that it is a country in a very hot, dry desert, but the River Nile - the longest river in the world - flows through it, bringing water and rich soil that allowed people to grow food and build one of the earliest great civilisations

pt-BR.name: Vida cotidiana no Egito Antigo
pt-BR.description: Descrever o dia a dia de pessoas comuns no Egito Antigo: agricultores plantando trigo e cevada perto do Nilo, casas de tijolos de barro, crianças brincando e com animais de estimação, alimentação com pão, peixe, frutas e legumes.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Everyday Life in Ancient Egypt
en.description: Describe what everyday life was like for ordinary people in ancient Egypt: farmers grew wheat and barley near the Nile, families lived in mud-brick houses, children played games and had pets, and people ate bread, fish, fruit, and vegetables

pt-BR.name: Hieróglifos e papiro
pt-BR.description: Saber que os antigos egípcios usavam um sistema de escrita com figuras e símbolos que representavam sons e palavras, os hieróglifos, escritos em papiro, material feito de uma planta que crescia às margens do Nilo.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Hieroglyphs and Papyrus
en.description: Know that the ancient Egyptians used a special writing system called hieroglyphs - pictures and symbols that stood for sounds and words - and that they wrote on a paper-like material called papyrus, which was made from a plant that grew along the Nile

pt-BR.name: Faraós e Tutancâmon
pt-BR.description: Saber que o Egito Antigo era governado por reis e rainhas poderosos, os faraós, que viviam em grandes palácios e faziam as leis, e que Tutancâmon, um menino que virou faraó, tem uma tumba de ouro descoberta milênios depois.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Pharaohs and Tutankhamun
en.description: Know that ancient Egypt was ruled by powerful kings and queens called pharaohs, who lived in grand palaces and made the laws - and that one of the most famous pharaohs is Tutankhamun, a boy who became pharaoh as a child and whose golden tomb was discovered thousands of years later

pt-BR.name: Pirâmides e a Grande Esfinge
pt-BR.description: Saber que os egípcios construíram enormes pirâmides de pedra como tumbas dos faraós, que a Grande Pirâmide de Gizé é uma das Sete Maravilhas do Mundo Antigo e que a Grande Esfinge, com corpo de leão e cabeça humana, a guarda.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Pyramids and the Great Sphinx
en.description: Know that the ancient Egyptians built enormous stone pyramids as tombs for the pharaohs, that the Great Pyramid at Giza was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World and is still standing today, and that the Great Sphinx - a statue with a lion's body and a human head - guards the pyramids

pt-BR.name: Vocabulário: Egito Antigo
pt-BR.description: Conhecer e usar o vocabulário-chave do Egito Antigo (faraó, pirâmide, tumba, múmia, hieróglifos, papiro, sarcófago, vaso canopo, natrão, arqueólogo, Nilo, delta, irrigação, escriba, vizir, obelisco, esfinge, cartucho) para descrever sociedade, religião e cultura material.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Vocabulary: ancient egypt
en.description: Know and use the key vocabulary of ancient Egypt - pharaoh, pyramid, tomb, mummy/mummification, hieroglyphs, papyrus, sarcophagus, canopic jar, natron, archaeologist, artefact, Nile, delta, irrigation, shaduf, scribe, vizier, obelisk, sphinx, cartouche - and apply these terms accurately when describing Egyptian society, religion, and material culture

pt-BR.name: O Egito Antigo na linha do tempo
pt-BR.description: Situar o Egito Antigo numa linha do tempo de mais de 3.000 anos, de cerca de 3100 a.C. (unificação) até 30 a.C. (conquista romana), e reconhecer seus grandes períodos: Antigo, Médio e Novo Império.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Ancient Egypt on the Timeline
en.description: Place ancient Egypt on a timeline spanning over 3,000 years - from around 3100 BCE (unification under the first pharaoh) to 30 BCE (Roman conquest) - understanding that this civilisation lasted longer than the time between the Romans and today, and was divided into major periods: the Old Kingdom (pyramid age), Middle Kingdom, and New Kingdom (empire age)

pt-BR.name: A construção das pirâmides
pt-BR.description: Entender como as pirâmides foram construídas: milhares de trabalhadores moviam blocos com rampas, rolos e trenós, sob organização de funcionários do faraó, e o projeto evoluiu das mastabas às pirâmides de degraus e à Grande Pirâmide, até as tumbas ocultas do Vale dos Reis.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Building the Pyramids
en.description: Understand how the pyramids were built: thousands of workers moved enormous stone blocks using ramps, rollers, and sledges, the work was organised by the pharaoh's officials, and the design evolved from flat-topped mastabas to step pyramids (like Djoser's) to the smooth-sided Great Pyramid - and know that later pharaohs were buried in hidden rock-cut tombs in the Valley of the Kings

pt-BR.name: Deuses e deusas do Egito
pt-BR.description: Nomear e descrever os principais deuses egípcios: Rá (sol), Osíris (além), Ísis (magia e maternidade), Anúbis (mumificação), Hórus (céu), Tot (escrita) e Bastet (proteção).
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Egyptian Gods and Goddesses
en.description: Name and describe key Egyptian gods and goddesses: Ra the sun god who sailed across the sky each day, Osiris the ruler of the afterlife, Isis the goddess of magic and motherhood, Anubis the jackal-headed god of mummification, Horus the falcon-headed sky god, Thoth the ibis-headed god of writing, and Bastet the cat goddess of protection

pt-BR.name: Hierarquia social no Egito
pt-BR.description: Descrever um modelo simplificado da hierarquia social egípcia: faraó, sacerdotes e nobres, escribas e soldados, artesãos e comerciantes, agricultores e trabalhadores. A origem familiar influenciava trabalho e oportunidades, mas havia mobilidade.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Egyptian Social Hierarchy
en.description: Describe a simplified model of ancient Egyptian social hierarchy: the pharaoh at the top, then priests and nobles, followed by scribes and soldiers, then craftworkers and merchants, with farmers and labourers at the base. Family background and status often shaped people’s work, resources and opportunities, while some people could move to a different position.

pt-BR.name: Pinturas de tumbas e objetos egípcios
pt-BR.description: Usar pinturas de tumbas, objetos e artefatos do Egito Antigo como evidência do cotidiano: as pinturas de Nebamun mostram caça e festas, joias e móveis revelam o artesanato e panelas e ferramentas mostram o uso comum.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Egyptian Tomb Paintings and Artefacts
en.description: Use tomb paintings, artefacts, and objects from ancient Egypt as evidence to find out about daily life: Nebamun's tomb paintings show hunting and feasting, jewellery and furniture reveal craftsmanship, and everyday objects like pots and tools tell us what ordinary people used - understanding that these sources are how we piece together information about a civilisation that ended thousands of years ago

pt-BR.name: Mumificação passo a passo
pt-BR.description: Descrever as etapas da mumificação: lavar o corpo, retirar os órgãos e guardá-los em vasos canopos, secar com natrão por 40 dias, enfaixar com linho e amuletos e colocar num caixão decorado (sarcófago).
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Mummification Step by Step
en.description: Describe the step-by-step process of mummification: the body was washed, internal organs were removed and placed in canopic jars, the body was dried with natron salt for 40 days, then wrapped in linen bandages with amulets tucked between the layers, and finally placed in a decorated coffin (sarcophagus)

pt-BR.name: Escribas e a Pedra de Roseta
pt-BR.description: Saber que escribas eram pessoas treinadas para ler e escrever hieróglifos, que a Pedra de Roseta traz o mesmo texto em três escritas e que Champollion a usou para decifrar os hieróglifos em 1822.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Scribes and the Rosetta Stone
en.description: Know that scribes were specially trained people who could read and write hieroglyphs, that the Rosetta Stone - a slab with the same text in three scripts - was the key to cracking the hieroglyphic code, and that Jean-François Champollion used it to decipher hieroglyphs in 1822 after centuries of mystery

pt-BR.name: Alto e Baixo Egito
pt-BR.description: Entender que o Egito era dividido em Alto Egito (vale estreito, ao sul) e Baixo Egito (delta largo, ao norte), unidos sob um faraó, e que a água do Nilo era controlada por canais de irrigação e shadufs para cultivar o ano todo.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Upper and Lower Egypt
en.description: Understand that ancient Egypt was divided into Upper Egypt (the narrow river valley in the south) and Lower Egypt (the wide delta in the north), that the two lands were united under one pharaoh, and that Egyptians managed the Nile's water through irrigation canals and shadufs to grow crops year-round

pt-BR.name: O legado duradouro do Egito Antigo
pt-BR.description: Avaliar o legado do Egito: medicina, matemática (usada nas pirâmides e na medição de terras após cheias), astronomia (calendário), engenharia, influência sobre Grécia e Roma e comparação com outras civilizações antigas (Mesopotâmia, Vale do Indo, dinastia Shang).
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Ancient Egypt's Lasting Legacy
en.description: Evaluate ancient Egypt's lasting legacy: the Egyptians developed early forms of medicine, mathematics (used to build pyramids and survey land after floods), astronomy (calendar based on star observations), and engineering that influenced later civilisations including Greece and Rome - and compare ancient Egypt with other early civilisations (Mesopotamia, Indus Valley, Shang Dynasty) to identify shared features like writing, agriculture, cities, and organised religion

pt-BR.name: Cleópatra e o fim do Egito
pt-BR.description: Saber que o Egito Antigo terminou quando Cleópatra VII, última faraó, aliada de Roma, foi derrotada por Otaviano em 31 a.C. e o Egito virou província do Império Romano, encerrando mais de 3.000 anos de governo faraônico.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Cleopatra and the End of Egypt
en.description: Know that ancient Egypt eventually came to an end: the last pharaoh was Cleopatra VII, who allied with Rome but was defeated by Octavian (later Augustus) in 31 BCE, after which Egypt became a province of the Roman Empire - ending over 3,000 years of pharaonic rule and beginning a new chapter in Egypt's history

pt-BR.name: Arte e arquitetura egípcias
pt-BR.description: Analisar a arte e a arquitetura egípcias: convenções da pintura (pessoas de lado com olhos de frente, tamanho indicando importância) e a evolução de mastabas a pirâmides e templos como Abu Simbel e Karnak, símbolos do poder do faraó e da devoção aos deuses.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Egyptian Art and Architecture
en.description: Analyse Egyptian art and architecture: understand that Egyptian paintings followed strict conventions (people shown from the side with eyes from the front, size indicating importance), that tomb and temple design evolved from mastabas to step pyramids to smooth pyramids to rock-cut temples like Abu Simbel, and that obelisks, colossal statues, and temples like Karnak demonstrated the pharaoh's power and devotion to the gods

pt-BR.name: Comércio e economia no Egito
pt-BR.description: Entender que a economia egípcia se baseava no excedente agrícola, no comércio e na especialização do trabalho, e que o Egito trocava ouro, papiro e grãos por cedro do Líbano, lápis-lazúli do Afeganistão e incenso de Punt.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Egyptian Trade and Economy
en.description: Understand that ancient Egypt had a thriving economy based on farming surplus, trade, and specialised labour: the Nile's fertile soil produced enough food to support craftworkers, priests, and officials, and Egypt traded along the Nile and across the Mediterranean - exchanging gold, papyrus, and grain for cedarwood from Lebanon, lapis lazuli from Afghanistan, and incense from Punt

pt-BR.name: O julgamento dos mortos
pt-BR.description: Descrever a crença egípcia no julgamento dos mortos: o coração era pesado contra a pena de Maat; coração puro levava ao paraíso (Campo de Juncos) e coração pesado era devorado por Ammit; o Livro dos Mortos trazia feitiços para ajudar na prova.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Judgement of the Dead
en.description: Describe the Egyptian belief in the judgement of the dead: after death, the heart was weighed against the feather of Ma'at in the Hall of Judgement, with Anubis overseeing the scales and Thoth recording the result - a pure heart meant entry to the Field of Reeds (paradise), while a heavy heart was devoured by the monster Ammit, and know that the Book of the Dead contained spells to help the deceased pass this test

pt-BR.name: Mapas do Egito Antigo
pt-BR.description: Interpretar mapas do Egito Antigo que mostram o Nilo, o delta, rotas comerciais e sítios importantes como Mênfis, Tebas e o Vale dos Reis.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Maps of ancient Egypt
en.description: Interpret maps of ancient Egypt showing the Nile, the Nile delta, trade routes and the location of key sites such as Memphis, Thebes and the Valley of the Kings

pt-BR.name: O faraó como deus vivo
pt-BR.description: Entender que o faraó era visto como deus vivo, intermediário entre deuses e povo, que a ideia de Maat (verdade, justiça e ordem) orientava leis e governo, e que vizires e funcionários administravam o reino em seu nome.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: The Pharaoh as Living God
en.description: Understand that the pharaoh was not just a ruler but was believed to be a living god - the intermediary between the gods and the people - and that the concept of Ma'at (truth, justice, and cosmic order) guided Egyptian law and government, with viziers and officials administering the kingdom on the pharaoh's behalf

pt-BR.name: Arqueologia moderna e ética no Egito
pt-BR.description: Entender que egiptólogos usam tomografia de múmias, imagens de satélite e análise de DNA além da escavação tradicional, e refletir criticamente sobre a ética: exibir múmias em museus, quem é dono dos artefatos e o efeito da coleta colonial.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Modern Archaeology and Egyptian Ethics
en.description: Understand that modern Egyptologists use advanced technologies - CT scanning of mummies, satellite imagery to find buried structures, DNA analysis - alongside traditional excavation, and think critically about the ethics of archaeology: whether mummies should be displayed in museums, who owns ancient artefacts, and how colonial-era collecting affects how we study and present ancient Egypt today

pt-BR.name: Matemática e engenharia egípcias
pt-BR.description: Descrever as conquistas egípcias em matemática e engenharia: o Papiro de Rhind (áreas, volumes, frações), o alinhamento preciso das pirâmides e os papiros médicos, com conhecimento anatômico e remédios.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Egyptian Maths and Engineering
en.description: Describe the Egyptian achievement in mathematics and engineering: the Rhind Mathematical Papyrus shows calculations of area, volume, and fractions; the precision of pyramid alignment (within 0.05° of true north) required sophisticated surveying; and Egyptian medical papyri describe detailed anatomical knowledge and pharmacological remedies - placing Egypt as a major contributor to the early history of science and technology

pt-BR.name: Fontes históricas sobre o Egito Antigo
pt-BR.description: Explicar como o conhecimento sobre o Egito se constrói com inscrições, papiros, artefatos e vestígios físicos, avaliando vieses e lacunas de cada fonte, o impacto da decifração dos hieróglifos por Champollion e por que um mesmo objeto pode ser interpretado de modos diferentes.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Historical Sources on Ancient Egypt
en.description: Explain how knowledge of ancient Egypt is built from multiple source types - inscriptions, papyri, artefacts, and physical remains - and critically evaluate each: what biases, gaps, and distortions exist? Explore how Champollion’s decipherment of hieroglyphs transformed the field, and why the same artefact can be interpreted differently by different scholars

pt-BR.name: O Egito e seus vizinhos
pt-BR.description: Examinar as relações do Egito com vizinhos: comércio com a Núbia, o Levante e Punt, a invasão dos hicsos e o carro de guerra, o império do Novo Reino e o conflito com os hititas, com a Batalha de Kadesh e o mais antigo tratado de paz conhecido.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Egypt and Its Neighbours
en.description: Examine Egypt's relationships with neighbouring civilisations: trade networks reaching Nubia, the Levant, and Punt; the Hyksos invasion and the introduction of the chariot; and the New Kingdom empire and its conflict with the Hittites, culminating in the Battle of Kadesh and the world's earliest surviving peace treaty - understanding Egypt not as isolated but as part of a connected ancient world

pt-BR.name: Quem realmente construiu as pirâmides
pt-BR.description: Analisar quem construiu as pirâmides e por quê, avaliando as evidências contra o mito dos alienígenas e o mito do trabalho escravo: vilas de operários em Gizé mostram mão de obra paga, qualificada e bem alimentada; a construção também tinha funções sociais e religiosas.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Who Really Built the Pyramids
en.description: Analyse who built the pyramids and why, evaluating the evidence against the alien-builder myth and the slave-labour myth: archaeological evidence from worker villages at Giza shows a paid, skilled, well-fed workforce; discuss the social functions of monument building as a form of state organisation, religious duty, and employment; and assess the current controversy over newly discovered construction ramps and logistics

pt-BR.name: A queda da civilização egípcia
pt-BR.description: Traçar o fim da civilização egípcia pelas conquistas assíria, persa, macedônica (Alexandre) e romana, mostrando como os conquistadores também foram influenciados pela cultura egípcia; examinar Cleópatra VII e o que sobrevive do Egito na cultura, religião e língua atuais.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Fall of Ancient Egyptian Civilisation
en.description: Trace the end of ancient Egyptian civilisation through its successive conquests - Assyrian, Persian, Macedonian (Alexander the Great), and finally Roman - and explain how each conqueror was simultaneously shaped by Egyptian culture; examine Cleopatra VII as the last pharaoh and as a multilingual political strategist; and consider what survives of ancient Egypt in modern culture, religion, and language

pt-BR.name: Grécia e Roma Antigas no mapa
pt-BR.description: Localizar a Grécia e a Itália no mapa e saber que, ao redor do Mar Mediterrâneo, cresceram há milhares de anos duas grandes civilizações, a Grécia e a Roma Antigas, muito depois do Egito e muito antes de nós.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Ancient Greece and Rome on the Map
en.description: Locate Greece and Italy on a map and know they are countries around the Mediterranean Sea where two great ancient civilisations - Ancient Greece and Ancient Rome - grew up thousands of years ago, long after the ancient Egyptians but long before our time

pt-BR.name: A vida antiga e a de hoje
pt-BR.description: Comparar a vida das crianças na Grécia ou em Roma antigas com a de hoje: escola (tabuinhas de cera, treino em Esparta), comida (azeitonas, pão, uvas), jogos e roupas (túnicas e sandálias), sabendo que isso foi há milhares de anos.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Ancient life vs today
en.description: Compare how children in ancient Greece or Rome lived with how children live today - including differences in school (writing on wax tablets, learning to fight in Sparta), food (olives, bread, grapes), games, and clothing (tunics and sandals) - and understand these civilisations existed thousands of years ago

pt-BR.name: Deuses gregos e o Monte Olimpo
pt-BR.description: Saber que os gregos antigos acreditavam em muitos deuses que viviam no Monte Olimpo, como Zeus (rei dos deuses, trovão), Atena (sabedoria), Poseidon (mar), Hermes (mensagens) e Afrodite (amor), cada um com poderes e papéis.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Greek gods & Mount Olympus
en.description: Know that the ancient Greeks believed in many gods and goddesses who lived on Mount Olympus - including Zeus (king of the gods, thunder), Athena (wisdom), Poseidon (the sea), Hermes (messages), and Aphrodite (love) - and that each god had special powers and a role in the world

pt-BR.name: Mitos e heróis gregos
pt-BR.description: Recontar ao menos um mito grego com herói e monstro, como Teseu e o Minotauro, Héracles e o leão ou Perseu e Medusa, entendendo que os gregos contavam essas histórias para explicar o mundo e ensinar lições.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Greek Myths and Heroes
en.description: Retell at least one Greek myth involving a hero and a monster - such as Theseus and the Minotaur in the labyrinth, Heracles (Hercules) and the lion, or Perseus and Medusa - and understand that these were stories ancient Greeks told to explain the world and teach lessons

pt-BR.name: Soldados e construtores romanos
pt-BR.description: Saber que soldados romanos marchavam por um império imenso construindo estradas retas e muralhas fortes, e que ainda se veem estradas, muros e edifícios romanos, sinal de grandes construtores.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Roman soldiers & builders
en.description: Know that Roman soldiers marched across a huge empire building straight roads and strong walls, and that some Roman roads, walls, and buildings can still be seen today - showing that the Romans were powerful builders whose work has lasted thousands of years

pt-BR.name: Rômulo e Remo
pt-BR.description: Conhecer o mito de fundação de Roma: os gêmeos Rômulo e Remo, abandonados bebês e criados por uma loba, que fundaram a cidade. Entender que é uma lenda contada pelos romanos.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Romulus & Remus
en.description: Know the Roman founding myth of Romulus and Remus - twin brothers abandoned as babies, raised by a she-wolf, who grew up to found the city of Rome - and understand that this is a legend the Romans told about how their city began

pt-BR.name: Os primeiros Jogos Olímpicos
pt-BR.description: Saber que os Jogos Olímpicos nasceram na Grécia Antiga, em Olímpia, como competições atléticas em honra a Zeus, e que os Jogos modernos se inspiraram neles.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: The first Olympics
en.description: Know that the Olympic Games began in ancient Greece at a place called Olympia as athletic competitions held in honour of Zeus, and that the modern Olympic Games we watch today were inspired by those ancient games

pt-BR.name: A democracia ateniense
pt-BR.description: Entender que Atenas criou a democracia, em que cidadãos homens livres reunidos na Assembleia debatiam e votavam as decisões da cidade, mas mulheres, escravizados e estrangeiros ficavam de fora.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Athenian Democracy
en.description: Understand that Athens invented democracy - a system where free male citizens gathered in an Assembly to debate and vote on important decisions for the city - but that women, enslaved people, and foreigners were not allowed to vote

pt-BR.name: Atenas e Esparta
pt-BR.description: Comparar Atenas e Esparta, duas cidades-Estado gregas muito diferentes: Atenas valorizava aprendizado, artes, debate e democracia; Esparta, treino militar, disciplina e obediência. Cidade-Estado é uma cidade que se governa como um pequeno país.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Athens Versus Sparta
en.description: Compare Athens and Sparta as two very different Greek city-states: Athens focused on learning, arts, debate, and democracy, while Sparta focused on military training, discipline, and obedience - and understand that a city-state was a city that ruled itself like a small country

pt-BR.name: A revolta de Boadiceia contra Roma
pt-BR.description: Contar a história de Boadiceia, rainha dos icenos, que liderou uma revolta contra o domínio romano na Britânia, incendiando Colchester, Londres e St Albans, até ser derrotada, e seu significado como símbolo de resistência.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Boudicca's Revolt Against Rome
en.description: Tell the story of Boudicca, queen of the Iceni tribe, who led a fierce revolt against Roman rule in Britain - burning Colchester, London, and St Albans - before her army was defeated, and understand her significance as a symbol of resistance against a powerful empire

pt-BR.name: A vida numa cidade romana
pt-BR.description: Descrever a vida numa cidade romana: o fórum, as termas, o anfiteatro e as vilas. Os romanos eram engenheiros brilhantes: estradas retas, aquedutos, aquecimento sob o piso (hipocausto) e a Muralha de Adriano na fronteira britânica.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Daily Life in a Roman Town
en.description: Describe daily life in a Roman town - the forum (marketplace and meeting place), public baths, amphitheatre, and villas - and explain that the Romans were brilliant engineers who built straight roads, aqueducts to carry water, underfloor heating (hypocaust), and Hadrian's Wall to mark the empire's northern frontier in Britain

pt-BR.name: Gladiadores e Pompeia
pt-BR.description: Saber que os romanos assistiam a lutas de gladiadores em arenas como o Coliseu, que os gladiadores eram em geral escravizados ou prisioneiros treinados, e que Pompeia foi soterrada pela erupção do Vesúvio em 79 d.C., preservando a vida cotidiana romana.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Gladiators & Pompeii
en.description: Know that Romans watched gladiators fight in huge arenas like the Colosseum in Rome, that gladiators were usually enslaved people or prisoners trained to fight, and that the city of Pompeii was buried by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in AD 79, preserving an extraordinary snapshot of Roman daily life

pt-BR.name: Os deuses e o Partenon
pt-BR.description: Nomear os principais deuses gregos e seus papéis (Zeus, Hera, Atena, Poseidon, Apolo, Ártemis, Ares, Afrodite, Hermes, Hefesto, Hades) e saber que o Partenon, em Atenas, era um grande templo em honra a Atena.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Gods & the Parthenon
en.description: Name the major Greek gods and their roles - Zeus (king, thunder), Hera (queen, marriage), Athena (wisdom, warfare), Poseidon (sea), Apollo (sun, music), Artemis (hunting, moon), Ares (war), Aphrodite (love), Hermes (messengers), Hephaestus (fire, crafts), Hades (underworld) - and know that the Parthenon in Athens was a grand temple built to honour Athena

pt-BR.name: Deuses gregos com nomes romanos
pt-BR.description: Entender que os romanos adotaram os deuses gregos com outros nomes (Zeus virou Júpiter, Hera virou Juno, Ares virou Marte, Atena virou Minerva, Poseidon virou Netuno, Afrodite virou Vênus), sinal da influência grega sobre Roma.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Greek Gods with Roman Names
en.description: Understand that the Romans adopted the Greek gods but gave them new names - Zeus became Jupiter, Hera became Juno, Ares became Mars, Athena became Minerva, Poseidon became Neptune, Aphrodite became Venus - and that this shows how deeply Rome was influenced by Greek culture

pt-BR.name: O teatro grego
pt-BR.description: Saber que os gregos antigos inventaram o teatro, com tragédias e comédias encenadas em grandes anfiteatros ao ar livre por atores com máscaras, em festivais religiosos em honra ao deus Dionísio, para plateias de milhares.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Greek theatre
en.description: Know that the ancient Greeks invented theatre, performing tragedies and comedies in large open-air amphitheatres with actors wearing masks - and that plays were performed as part of religious festivals honouring the god Dionysus, with audiences of thousands

pt-BR.name: Maratona e Termópilas
pt-BR.description: Descrever as batalhas de Maratona e Termópilas, em que as cidades-Estado gregas se uniram contra a invasão persa: o corredor Fidípides levando a notícia da vitória (origem da maratona) e a resistência dos 300 espartanos, em defesa da independência grega.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Marathon and Thermopylae
en.description: Describe the battles of Marathon and Thermopylae as moments when Greek city-states united against the invading Persian Empire - the runner Pheidippides bringing news of victory at Marathon (origin of the marathon race), and the heroic stand of 300 Spartans at Thermopylae - and understand these wars were fought to defend Greek independence

pt-BR.name: O exército romano e a conquista da Britânia
pt-BR.description: Descrever como o exército romano se organizava em legiões de soldados treinados, como Júlio César invadiu a Britânia em 55 a.C. e o imperador Cláudio a conquistou em 43 d.C., e por que Roma expandia o império: terras, recursos, impostos e glória.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Roman Army and Conquest of Britain
en.description: Describe how the Roman army was organised into legions of highly trained soldiers, how Julius Caesar first raided Britain in 55 BC and Emperor Claudius later conquered it in AD 43, and explain why the Romans wanted to expand their empire - for land, resources, taxes, and glory

pt-BR.name: O império de Alexandre, o Grande
pt-BR.description: Descrever como Alexandre da Macedônia conquistou um vasto império da Grécia ao Egito e à Índia, espalhando a língua e a cultura gregas e criando o período helenístico, de mistura das culturas grega e oriental.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Alexander the Great's Empire
en.description: Describe how Alexander the Great of Macedon conquered a vast empire stretching from Greece to Egypt to India, spreading Greek language, culture, and ideas across the ancient world - creating a period known as the Hellenistic Age where Greek and Eastern cultures blended

pt-BR.name: Evidências da vida grega e romana
pt-BR.description: Entender que historiadores e arqueólogos reconstroem a vida grega e romana por evidências (pinturas em vasos, moedas, inscrições, ruínas como Pompeia e textos de Homero e Plínio) e que a mesma evidência pode ser interpretada de modos diferentes.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Evidence for Greek and Roman Life
en.description: Understand that historians and archaeologists piece together ancient Greek and Roman life from evidence - pottery paintings, coins, inscriptions, ruins like Pompeii, and written texts by authors such as Homer and Pliny - and that the same evidence can be interpreted in different ways by different historians

pt-BR.name: A queda do Império Romano do Ocidente
pt-BR.description: Descrever como o Império Romano do Ocidente declinou por pressão de povos invasores, instabilidade política, problemas econômicos e excesso de extensão, caindo em 476 d.C., enquanto o Império Romano do Oriente (Bizantino) durou quase mil anos mais.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
en.description: Describe how the Western Roman Empire gradually declined due to a combination of factors - military pressure from invading peoples, political instability, economic problems, and an overstretched empire - and finally fell in AD 476, while the Eastern Roman (Byzantine) Empire continued for nearly a thousand more years

pt-BR.name: Arquitetura grega e romana
pt-BR.description: Identificar as colunas gregas (dórica, jônica e coríntia) e as inovações romanas (arco, cúpula e concreto) e reconhecer sua influência em prédios modernos, como fóruns, museus e monumentos.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Greek and Roman Architecture
en.description: Identify Greek column styles - Doric (plain and sturdy), Ionic (scroll-shaped capitals), and Corinthian (ornate leafy capitals) - and Roman architectural innovations - the arch, the dome, and concrete - and spot their influence in modern public buildings such as courthouses, museums, government buildings, and monuments

pt-BR.name: O legado grego e romano hoje
pt-BR.description: Avaliar as contribuições de gregos e romanos à vida moderna (democracia, direito, língua com raízes latinas, arquitetura, esporte, filosofia, literatura e teatro) e entender que as ideias gregas chegaram a nós por Roma e por civilizações europeias posteriores.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Greek and Roman Legacy Today
en.description: Evaluate the lasting contributions of Greek and Roman civilisations to modern life - democracy, law, language (Latin roots), architecture (columns, arches, domes), sport (Olympics), philosophy, literature, and theatre - and understand that Greek ideas reached us through Rome, and then through later European civilisations, in a chain of cultural transmission

pt-BR.name: Filósofos e medicina na Grécia
pt-BR.description: Saber que filósofos gregos criaram modos de entender o mundo que ainda nos influenciam: Sócrates e seu método de perguntas, Platão e a sociedade ideal, Aristóteles e a classificação da natureza, e Hipócrates, o pai da medicina, que buscava causas naturais das doenças.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Greek Philosophers and Medicine
en.description: Know that Greek thinkers called philosophers developed ways of understanding the world that still influence us today - Socrates asked challenging questions to test ideas (the Socratic method), Plato imagined the ideal society, Aristotle observed and classified the natural world - and that Hippocrates is called the father of medicine for insisting on natural causes of illness rather than blaming the gods

pt-BR.name: Direito romano, latim e cristianismo
pt-BR.description: Entender que o direito romano é base de sistemas jurídicos da Europa e de outros lugares, que o latim originou o português, o francês, o espanhol, o italiano e o romeno, e que o cristianismo se espalhou pelo Império até se tornar religião oficial com Constantino.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Roman Law, Latin, and Christianity
en.description: Understand that Roman law became the basis for legal systems across Europe and beyond, that Latin is the root of French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, and Romanian and gave English hundreds of words (e.g. exit, video, annual, education), and that Christianity spread throughout the Roman Empire, eventually becoming its official religion under Emperor Constantine

pt-BR.name: República e Império Romano
pt-BR.description: Explicar como Roma foi governada como república, com cônsules eleitos, Senado poderoso e distinção entre patrícios e plebeus, antes de virar império de imperadores como Augusto (Pax Romana) e Nero, e comparar com a democracia direta de Atenas.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Roman Republic and Empire
en.description: Explain how Rome was first governed as a republic - with elected consuls, a powerful Senate, and a distinction between patricians and plebeians - before becoming an empire ruled by emperors like Augustus (who brought peace, the Pax Romana) and Nero, and compare republican government with Athenian direct democracy

pt-BR.name: Vozes esquecidas na Grécia e em Roma
pt-BR.description: Examinar a vida de quem costuma ficar fora da história greco-romana: escravizados (cerca de 30% de Atenas), mulheres (diferentes em Atenas e em Esparta) e povos conquistados, avaliando quais vozes faltam nos registros e por quê.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Hidden Voices of Greece and Rome
en.description: Examine the lives of people usually left out of the Greek and Roman story - enslaved people who made up roughly 30% of Athens and powered Rome's economy, women whose lives varied dramatically between Athens (largely confined to the home) and Sparta (physical training, property ownership), and conquered peoples across both empires - and evaluate whose voices are missing from the historical record and why

pt-BR.name: Inclusão e exclusão em Atenas
pt-BR.description: Analisar quem participava da democracia ateniense (só homens adultos livres, cerca de 30% dos adultos) e quem era excluído (mulheres, escravizados e estrangeiros), avaliando se Atenas merece ser chamada de berço da democracia, em comparação com democracias representativas modernas.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Inclusion and Exclusion in Athens
en.description: Analyse who was included and excluded from Athenian democracy - only free adult male citizens (roughly 30% of adults) could participate, while women, enslaved people (who may have made up a third of the population), and foreign residents (metics) were excluded - and evaluate whether Athens truly deserves the title 'birthplace of democracy' by comparing it with modern representative democracies

pt-BR.name: Troia: mito ou história?
pt-BR.description: Explorar como a escavação de Schliemann em Hisarlik, na Turquia, levantou dúvidas sobre se a Guerra de Troia da Ilíada foi histórica, parcialmente histórica ou mito, entendendo que arqueologia e fontes literárias podem se apoiar ou se contradizer.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Troy: Myth or History?
en.description: Explore how Heinrich Schliemann's excavation at Hisarlik in modern Turkey raised questions about whether the Trojan War described in Homer's Iliad was historical, partly historical, or entirely mythical - understanding that archaeology and literary sources can support or contradict each other, and that the line between myth and history in the ancient world is often blurred

pt-BR.name: A queda da República Romana
pt-BR.description: Traçar como a violência política (morte dos Gracos, guerras entre Mário e Sula, Júlio César cruzando o Rubicão e seu assassinato nos Idos de Março, guerra entre Otaviano e Antônio) destruiu a República e levou ao poder de um só homem com Augusto, debatendo se era inevitável.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Fall of the Roman Republic
en.description: Trace how Roman political violence - the murder of the Gracchi brothers, civil wars between Marius and Sulla, Caesar's crossing of the Rubicon and assassination on the Ides of March, and the final war between Octavian and Antony - destroyed the Republic and led to one-man rule under Augustus, and debate whether the fall of the Republic was inevitable or a series of choices

pt-BR.name: Celebrações que compartilhamos
pt-BR.description: Descrever as celebrações e comemorações de acontecimentos importantes que compartilha com a família e outras pessoas e como são marcadas.
pt-BR.domain: História da família e da comunidade
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Celebrations we share
en.description: Describe the celebrations and commemorations of significant events that they share with their families and others, and how they are marked

pt-BR.name: Minha família e de onde viemos
pt-BR.description: Identificar as pessoas da família, onde nasceram e cresceram os familiares e como se relacionam entre si.
pt-BR.domain: História da família e da comunidade
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: My family and where we're from
en.description: Identify the people in their family, where family members were born and raised, and how they are related to each other

pt-BR.name: A infância antes e agora
pt-BR.description: Identificar continuidades e mudanças entre o dia a dia atual e a infância de pais e avós: escola, brincadeiras, brinquedos, tarefas, comida e tecnologia.
pt-BR.domain: História da família e da comunidade
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Childhood then and now
en.description: Identify continuity and change between aspects of their daily lives and their parents' and grandparents' childhoods, such as school, play, toys, chores, food and technology

pt-BR.name: Pessoas e lugares importantes da comunidade
pt-BR.description: Investigar uma pessoa, grupo, lugar ou edifício local e as razões de sua importância social, cultural ou espiritual.
pt-BR.domain: História da família e da comunidade
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Important local people and places
en.description: Investigate a local individual, group, place or building and the reasons for its importance, including social, cultural or spiritual significance

pt-BR.name: A tecnologia muda o nosso modo de viver
pt-BR.description: Descrever como o desenvolvimento tecnológico mudou a vida em casa e as formas de trabalhar, viajar e se comunicar.
pt-BR.domain: História da família e da comunidade
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Technology changes how we live
en.description: Describe how technological developments changed people's lives at home and the ways they worked, travelled and communicated

pt-BR.name: Como a nossa comunidade mudou
pt-BR.description: Identificar causas e efeitos de mudanças na comunidade local (nova ferrovia, novas moradias, migração, fechamento de fábrica) e como pessoas de origens diversas, incluindo povos originários e migrantes, contribuíram.
pt-BR.domain: História da família e da comunidade
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: How our community changed
en.description: Identify causes and effects of changes to the local community (e.g. a new railway, new housing, migration, a factory closing) and how people from diverse backgrounds, including First Nations Australians and migrants, have contributed to these changes

pt-BR.name: Datas nacionais e comemorações
pt-BR.description: Identificar dias importantes para a identidade e a diversidade da Austrália (Dia da Austrália, Anzac Day, Semana NAIDOC, Dia Nacional do Perdão) e como são lembrados ou reconhecidos.
pt-BR.domain: História da família e da comunidade
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: National days and commemorations
en.description: Identify significant days that are important to Australia's identity and diversity and how they are commemorated or recognised, including Australia Day, Anzac Day, NAIDOC Week and National Sorry Day

pt-BR.name: Linhas do tempo de acontecimentos passados
pt-BR.description: Reunir, ordenar e registrar informações sobre acontecimentos passados em linhas do tempo sem escala, colocando figuras ou eventos rotulados do mais antigo ao mais recente.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Timelines of past events
en.description: Collect, sort and record information about past events on unscaled timelines, placing pictures or labelled events in order from earliest to latest

pt-BR.name: Diferentes perspectivas e relatos
pt-BR.description: Reconhecer que pessoas diferentes podem ter perspectivas e relatos diferentes sobre o mesmo objeto, lugar ou acontecimento, e que ambos podem ser sinceros e ainda assim discordar.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Different perspectives and accounts
en.description: Recognise that different people can have different perspectives on, and give different accounts of, the same object, place or event - and that both can be genuine while still disagreeing

pt-BR.name: Evidências do passado
pt-BR.description: Entender que tudo o que sabemos do passado vem de evidências que sobreviveram (objetos, edifícios, imagens, documentos e histórias) e usar pistas delas para descobrir como as pessoas viviam.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Evidence from the Past
en.description: Understand that everything we know about the past comes from evidence that has survived - objects, buildings, pictures, documents and stories - and use clues in that evidence to work out how people lived

pt-BR.name: Perguntas sobre o passado
pt-BR.description: Formular perguntas sobre objetos, pessoas, lugares e acontecimentos do passado e do presente, como quem usava um objeto, como era um lugar antigamente ou como se celebrava um evento.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Questions about the past
en.description: Develop questions about objects, people, places and events in the past and present, such as who used an object, what a place was like long ago or how an event was celebrated

pt-BR.name: Vocabulário: pensamento histórico
pt-BR.description: Conhecer e usar o vocabulário do pensamento histórico (fonte, evidência, fonte primária e secundária, artefato, cronologia, a.C./d.C., século, década, era, período, linha do tempo, escavação, interpretação, viés, perspectiva) para falar de como sabemos sobre o passado.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Vocabulary: historical thinking
en.description: Know and use the vocabulary of historical thinking - source, evidence, primary source, secondary source, artefact, chronology, chronological order, BC/BCE, AD/CE, century, decade, era, period, timeline, excavation, archaeologist, interpretation, corroborate, bias, perspective - and apply these terms when discussing how we know about the past and how reliable our knowledge is

pt-BR.name: Conferir fontes entre si
pt-BR.description: Corroborar: verificar se várias fontes concordam sobre os mesmos fatos e investigar por que podem discordar.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Checking Sources Against Each Other
en.description: Corroborate: check whether multiple sources agree on the same facts - and investigate why they might not

pt-BR.name: Linhas do tempo datadas com notas
pt-BR.description: Localizar, reunir e registrar informações de várias fontes em linhas do tempo com datas, escala adequada e uma breve nota e fonte para cada evento.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Dated timelines with notes
en.description: Locate, collect and record information from a range of sources on annotated timelines with dates, an appropriate scale and a brief note and source for each event

pt-BR.name: Questionar as fontes históricas
pt-BR.description: Antes de confiar numa fonte histórica, perguntar quem a fez, quando e por quê, pois as respostas determinam o peso que ela deve ter.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Questioning Historical Sources
en.description: Before trusting a historical source, ask: who made this, when, and why? - the answers shape how much weight the source should carry

pt-BR.name: Entender as pessoas em seu próprio tempo
pt-BR.description: Entender que as pessoas do passado viam o mundo de modo muito diferente do nosso e julgar suas ações pelo contexto em que viviam, não só pelos valores de hoje.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Understanding People in Their Own Time
en.description: Understand that people in the past saw the world very differently from us - judge their actions by the context they lived in, not only by today's values

pt-BR.name: Evidência versus interpretação
pt-BR.description: Distinguir evidência histórica (o que sobreviveu) de interpretação (o argumento que o historiador constrói), reconhecendo que a mesma evidência pode sustentar argumentos diferentes.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Evidence Versus Interpretation
en.description: Distinguish between historical evidence and historical interpretation - evidence is what survived, interpretation is the argument a historian builds from it, and the same evidence can support different arguments

pt-BR.name: Reis e rainhas
pt-BR.description: O que faziam reis e rainhas medievais: governar, fazer leis e cobrar impostos; coroa e trono como símbolos de poder; a Torre de Londres.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Kings & Queens
en.description: What medieval kings and queens did: ruling the land, making laws, collecting taxes; the crown and throne as symbols of power; the Tower of London

pt-BR.name: Cavaleiros e armaduras
pt-BR.description: O que eram cavaleiros: guerreiros treinados a serviço de um senhor; armaduras, escudos, espadas e lanças; o código de cavalaria como regras de conduta.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Knights & Armour
en.description: What knights were: trained warriors who served a lord; armour, shields, swords, and lances; the code of chivalry as rules for how knights should behave

pt-BR.name: Roupas medievais
pt-BR.description: O que as pessoas vestiam na Idade Média: roupas de camponeses (lã e linho) e de nobres (seda, peles, cores vivas); sem zíperes nem botões; como a roupa indicava a posição social.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Medieval Clothing
en.description: What people wore in medieval times: peasant clothes (wool, linen) vs noble clothes (silk, fur, bright colours); no zippers or buttons; how clothes showed your place in society

pt-BR.name: Comida e banquetes medievais
pt-BR.description: O que as pessoas comiam na Idade Média: pão e ensopado para o povo, banquetes para os ricos; sem garfos, comendo com as mãos; o grande salão como centro da vida no castelo.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Medieval Food & Feasts
en.description: What people ate in medieval times: bread and pottage for ordinary people, grand feasts for the rich; no forks, eating with hands; the great hall as the centre of castle life

pt-BR.name: Robin Hood e Rei Arthur
pt-BR.description: As lendas de Robin Hood (Floresta de Sherwood, roubar dos ricos, os Merry Men) e do Rei Arthur (Távola Redonda, Excalibur, Camelot); são histórias, não história comprovada, mas refletem valores medievais.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Robin Hood & King Arthur
en.description: The legends of Robin Hood (Sherwood Forest, stealing from the rich, Merry Men) and King Arthur (Round Table, Excalibur, Camelot); that these are stories, not proven history, but reflect medieval values

pt-BR.name: Os vikings
pt-BR.description: Quem eram os vikings: guerreiros navegadores e comerciantes da Escandinávia, seus barcos longos, os ataques à Britânia e o fato de também se fixarem e cultivarem a terra.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: The Vikings
en.description: Who the Vikings were: seafaring warriors and traders from Scandinavia; longships; Viking raids on Britain; that Vikings also settled and farmed

pt-BR.name: A vida na aldeia
pt-BR.description: O cotidiano de pessoas comuns numa aldeia medieval: casas de palha, lavoura, assar pão, buscar água, e como era diferente de hoje.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Village Life
en.description: Daily life for ordinary people in a medieval village: thatched houses, farming, baking bread, fetching water; how different life was from today

pt-BR.name: O que é um castelo
pt-BR.description: O que é um castelo: edifício fortificado usado como moradia e defesa; partes principais (torres, fosso, ponte levadiça, muros grossos) e motivos para sua construção.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: What Is a Castle?
en.description: What a castle is: a fortified building used as both a home and a defence; key parts including towers, moat, drawbridge, and thick walls; why castles were built

pt-BR.name: A Britânia anglo-saxônica
pt-BR.description: Quem eram os anglo-saxões: povos germânicos que se instalaram na Britânia após a saída dos romanos; seus reinos, aldeias, nomes de lugares, arte e a conversão ao cristianismo.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Anglo-Saxon Britain
en.description: Who the Anglo-Saxons were: Germanic peoples who settled in Britain after the Romans left; their kingdoms, villages, place names, art, and eventual conversion to Christianity

pt-BR.name: A Batalha de Hastings e o ano de 1066
pt-BR.description: Os acontecimentos de 1066: morte de Eduardo, o Confessor, três pretendentes ao trono, a Batalha de Hastings, Guilherme, o Conquistador, e a Tapeçaria de Bayeux como fonte histórica.
pt-BR.sourceAgent: Code/Claude

en.name: Battle of Hastings and 1066
en.description: The events of 1066: the death of Edward the Confessor, three claimants to the throne, the Battle of Hastings, William the Conqueror, and the Bayeux Tapestry as a historical source

pt-BR.name: Projeto de castelos ao longo do tempo
